source_name: Diebold Nixdorf newsroom / IR document archive
why_relevant: Primary ATM/branch-automation and retail checkout vendor in CEE; announces ATM-as-a-Service and hardware refresh wins that are otherwise invisible for private banks and retailers.

source_name: NCR Atleos / NCR Voyix newsroom
why_relevant: Second global ATM/self-service and retail POS vendor pair; Hungarian bank ATM fleet and retail self-checkout wins typically surface only in their releases or in ATM Marketplace coverage.

source_name: ATM Marketplace (vendor-announcement aggregator)
why_relevant: Aggregates ATM/self-service vendor press releases by company, giving a single sweep point for Diebold Nixdorf, NCR, Euronet, Hyosung deals touching Hungary.

source_name: Asseco Case Study Book — Banking & Capital Market
why_relevant: Asseco is a major CEE banking-software group with a Hungarian subsidiary; its case-study book names bank customers (incl. CIB Bank Hungary mobile banking, OTP CrediLogic) that never appear in any procurement register.

source_name: Asseco Magyarország (Hungarian subsidiary site)
why_relevant: Local-language vendor site listing Hungarian financial-sector products and references (e.g. CrediLogic at OTP since 2004); Hungarian-language news/referencia pages carry deals not translated into English.

source_name: Comarch Finance case studies
why_relevant: Polish CEE vendor active in banking/insurance across the region; case-study library is the disclosure channel for bank platform wins, including regional groups with Hungarian units (e.g. ING).

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. sajtóközlemények (Hungarian IT integrator)
why_relevant: Largest listed Hungarian IT integrator; publishes Hungarian-language press releases and BSE disclosures on contract wins including financial-sector infrastructure — a domestic seller-side award notice channel.

source_name: DSS Consulting blog / referenciák
why_relevant: Hungarian banking-software house that publicly describes winning a public procurement tender to rebuild a leading Hungarian bank's regulatory reporting system — exactly the seller-side disclosure of an otherwise unnamed deal.

source_name: MINDSPIRE banki transzformációs blog / project pages
why_relevant: Hungarian banking-transformation consultancy that publishes status overviews of which Hungarian banks are replacing core systems and with which platforms (Flexcube, T24, Murex), plus its own AFR instant-payment project involvement — a rare aggregated view of live vendor selections.

source_name: FinTech Futures — Hungary keyword feed
why_relevant: Curated stream of Hungary-tagged banking-technology stories, most of which originate as vendor press releases; the fastest way to discover new vendor-win announcements and the vendors behind them.

source_name: IBS Intelligence news
why_relevant: Banking-technology deal tracker; systematically reports vendor-bank contract signings including Hungarian ones, and its IBS Sales League Table is a structured record of who sold what where.

source_name: Financial IT news
why_relevant: Republishes vendor press releases near-verbatim, often earlier than filtered trade press; useful to catch vendor announcements whose own newsroom is hard to crawl.

source_name: The Paypers — payments vendor deal news
why_relevant: Dense coverage of payment-vendor contract announcements across Europe including CEE; good snowball source for acquiring, issuing, fraud and open-banking vendors serving Hungary.

source_name: GK Software newsroom (retail POS)
why_relevant: Won Lidl's group-wide POS software modernisation (Cloud4Retail) rolled out across ~30 countries including Hungary; retail POS vendor releases are the only public trace of Hungarian store-checkout platform changes.

source_name: OTP Mobil / SimplePay and Barion corporate news (HU payment providers)
why_relevant: Domestic PSPs whose Hungarian-language announcements reveal merchant wins, acquisitions (Barion acquiring PSC CEE for offline/merchant services) and Qvik instant-payment integrations — vendor-side evidence of Hungarian retailer and bank payment deals.

source_name: ITBusiness.hu (itbo.hu)
why_relevant: Second Hungarian IT trade outlet covering enterprise/banking IT deployments and vendor announcements in Hungarian; complements Bitport for local vendor-win discovery.

source_name: Smartsector referenciák (HU financial-sector IT vendor)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language vendor reference page naming financial-sector clients; representative of a whole tier of small domestic suppliers whose 'referenciáink' pages are the only public record of their bank contracts.

source_name: Broadcom/Symantec customer case study archive (Budapest Bank example)
why_relevant: Demonstrates that security/fraud vendors publish named Hungarian bank case studies (Budapest Bank) as PDFs on documentation CDNs rather than in newsrooms — an easily missed disclosure surface for fraud/security deals.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (Hungarian e-procurement platform)
why_relevant: Mandatory national platform where Hungarian contracting authorities run procedures and publish notices. Structured search by CPV code, subject and place of performance was extended in 2024, so integrator-facing IT/banking-adjacent lots (CPV 72xxx, 48xxx, 66xxx) can be filtered and monitored. This is where 4iG, T-Systems, Delta, NTT Data HU etc. appear as bidders/winners on public-sector IT and payment-related contracts.

source_name: OpenTender Hungary (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Cleaned, deduplicated merge of TED and the Hungarian national portal, covering both above- and below-threshold contracts, with supplier profiles and downloadable datasets (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Lets you build a supplier-level history for 4iG, T-Systems HU, Delta, NTT Data HU, consultancies, without re-scraping raw notices.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. investor relations – annual and quarterly reports
why_relevant: Hungary's dominant listed system integrator. Its consolidated IFRS reports and gyorsjelentés (quarterly flash reports) segment revenue by IT system integration vs telecom vs defence and name major engagements — including state financial infrastructure work (e.g. the Hungarian State Treasury account-management and accounting system replacement). Primary disclosure of framework-contract exposure to public buyers.

source_name: BÉT / BSE KIB regulatory disclosure feed (bet.hu newkibdata)
why_relevant: Budapest Stock Exchange's mandatory-disclosure store carries the same integrator filings (4iG, Magyar Telekom/T-Systems parent, Delta Technologies) plus material-event announcements about contract wins and state investigations — often published here before company websites. Structured, dated, and durable.

source_name: NISZ Zrt. közadat – supplier contract register (5 M HUF+ contracts)
why_relevant: State IT operator publishes, as mandatory public-interest data, a line-item list of supplier contracts above HUF 5 million with supplier name, description, framework amount and signature date. A rare, direct, structured view of which integrators and software houses actually deliver into central government (and financial-administration) systems, downloadable as PDF/XLS.

source_name: ITBusiness.hu – Hungarian enterprise IT trade magazine
why_relevant: Publishes vendor-sourced project announcements, integrator rankings and 'cégvilág' pieces naming which integrator became market leader and which deals drove it. Vendor press releases here often name bank clients that never appear in procurement records (private-sector deals).

source_name: PwC Magyarország sajtószoba (press room) – payments & digital finance studies
why_relevant: Big-Four consultancy press room publishing HU-specific payments/digitalisation studies (e.g. 'Digitális fordulat a hazai pénzforgalomban', 2025). Doubles as an indirect signal of where the firm is selling: study topics track their live banking engagements. Also names bank participants.

source_name: Deloitte Magyarország – banking/technology insights and Digital Banking Maturity
why_relevant: Deloitte HU publishes recurring banking-digitalisation research (Digital Banking Maturity, Deloitte Digital HU customer studies) that benchmarks Hungarian banks and signals the firm's consulting footprint in the sector. Note the site is mid-migration between deloitte.com/hu and www2.deloitte.com/hu — both paths carry live content.

source_name: KPMG Magyarország press releases + KPMG Blog (digitális transzformáció tag)
why_relevant: KPMG HU press releases and its blog's digital-transformation tag track advisory positioning in HU financial services; KPMG HU also publishes structural sector inventories (e.g. its SSC CEE Network list of shared service centres) useful for mapping which financial institutions run delivery centres in HU/CEE and who serves them.
